skill.name: prototype
skill.description: Build a throwaway prototype to flush out a design before committing to it. Routes between two branches — a runnable terminal app for state/business-logic questions, or several radically different UI variations toggleable from one route. Use when the user wants to prototype, sanity-check a data model or state machine, mock up a UI, explore design options, or says "prototype this", "let me play with it", "try a few designs".
skill.summary: Build disposable logic or UI prototypes before committing to a design.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Teams often commit to state models or screens before they understand the tradeoffs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to build disposable prototypes that answer one design question quickly.
actual_capabilities: Chooses between logic and UI prototype workflows based on the user question.
Creates interactive terminal prototypes for state models and business logic.
Creates multiple UI variants behind one route and variant switcher.
Keeps prototypes close to the relevant module, page, or component.
Documents the question, run command, result, and cleanup path.
Uses the host project runtime, router, and task runner when available.
limitations: Designed for temporary exploration, not production-ready implementation.
Skips tests and broad error handling unless needed to run the prototype.
Needs project context to choose the right route, runtime, and task command.
May require user feedback to select a final UI variant or logic direction.

use_cases.title: Test State Models
use_cases.description: Build a small terminal prototype so edge cases are visible before the real implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Compare Page Directions
use_cases.description: Create several structurally different page variants that can be reviewed on the same route.

use_cases.title: Align Before Building
use_cases.description: Use a disposable prototype to turn an unclear requirement into a concrete decision.

prompt_templates.title: Prototype a State Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Prototype this state flow so I can try the main actions and see the state after each step.

prompt_templates.title: Explore UI Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three different UI variants for this page and let me switch between them in the browser.

prompt_templates.title: Mount Variants in Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the existing page and data, then add switchable prototype variants without changing production behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Product Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the smallest prototype that answers whether this workflow, state model, and screen structure fit together.

output_examples.input: Prototype the onboarding state machine before we write the production reducer.
output_examples.output: A local terminal prototype with visible state, keyboard actions, a run command, and notes for the final decision.

output_examples.input: Show three directions for the settings page using our existing layout.
output_examples.output: Three route-level variants, a bottom switcher, stable URL selection, and cleanup notes after a variant wins.

output_examples.input: Check whether the downgrade flow handles billing edge cases.
output_examples.output: A focused prototype that models the flow, exposes state changes, and records which assumptions failed.

best_practices: Start by writing the exact question the prototype must answer.
Use the existing project runtime, router, data shape, and task runner.
Delete the prototype or fold the validated decision into real code.
anti_patterns: Do not connect exploratory prototypes to production databases or real mutations.
Do not make UI variants that only differ in color or copy.
Do not leave throwaway routes, switchers, or terminal shells in production code.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a design, workflow, state model, or UI direction needs quick validation before implementation.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. It creates temporary code that should be deleted or rewritten after the decision is clear.

faq.question: Can it prototype backend logic?
faq.answer: Yes. It can build a terminal prototype around reducers, state machines, functions, or modules.

faq.question: Can it prototype UI screens?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create multiple route variants and a switcher for browser review.

faq.question: Does it require a specific framework?
faq.answer: No. It tells the assistant to use the host project's existing tools and conventions.

faq.question: What should remain after the prototype?
faq.answer: Only the answer, the chosen direction, and any real implementation that came from the validated idea should remain.
